newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices gain on hot weather, nukes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices gain on hot weather, nukes.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices moved higher again Monday, lifted by news of two unplanned nuclear plant outages in Pennsylvania and the season's first heat wave in the Midwest and Northeast, market sources said.
And traders said forecasts this week for more heat should keep physical prices fairly firm and set a more bullish tone during bidweek later in the week.

"We've got some burn and we still have some storage to catch up on, and as more heat comes in, I see higher prices," said one Texas trader. Louisiana Gulf Coast prices firmed almost five cents to the mid-to-high $2.20s per mmBtu.
PECO's 1,055 MW Limerick 1 nuclear power unit and GPU's 786 MW Three Mile Island 1 unit both were shut over the weekend for unscheduled repairs and were likely to remain down through the week.

These latest outages, added to long-term outages at two units at the Salem, New Jersey facility, and three units at the Millstone plant in Connecticut, could leave the area tight on generation this week and help prop up gas prices ahead of bidweek later in the week.
Spot electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic almost doubled Monday on news of the plant shutdowns amid the heat wave.

South Texas prices also gained nearly a nickel Monday to the high-teens. Though temperatures there have cooled because of clouds and showers, high humidity still fueled generation demand and warmer weather was expected later in the week.
In the East, New York city gate prices rallied almost a dime to the high-$2.50s. Temperatures in the Northeast are forecast to hover around 90 degrees F through the week with increasing humidity.

In the Midwest, prices were up an average of four cents to near the $2.10 level, but Chicago city-gate jumped more than a dime to about $2.40 on some heat in the area. Temperatures in the region are expected to remain above normal through the week.
Southern California prices also firmed a few cents into the mid-$2.20s.
